appraisal_events.evidence: quand Mme de Cambremer se demandait comment je pouvais délaisser pour Albertine un homme remarquable comme Elstir. Même au point de vue intellectuel je sentais qu'elle avait tort, mais je ne savais pas que ce qu'elle méconnaissait, c'était les leçons avec lesquelles on fait son apprentissage d'homme de lettres.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly asserts that Mme de Cambremer's implied criticism of his choosing Albertine over Elstir was intellectually wrong, revealing she misunderstood what literary apprenticeship actually requires; her judgment is locally diminished by this correction.

appraisal_events.evidence: Ma grand'mère que j'avais, avec tant d'indifférence, vue agoniser et mourir près de moi ! Ô puissé-je, en expiation, quand mon œuvre serait terminée, blessé sans remède, souffrir de longues heures abandonné de tous, avant de mourir.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator reproaches his own past indifference while watching his grandmother die and wishes for expiatory suffering, an explicit act of self-blame.

status_effects.explanation: Her judgment about the narrator's priorities is shown to rest on a misunderstanding of what shapes a writer's apprenticeship, locally lowering her standing as a perceptive evaluator.
The narrator's explicit guilt over his past indifference and his wish for expiatory suffering mark a sharp local diminishment in his own emotional standing.

ambiguities: The self-reproach concerning the grandmother targets the narrator himself rather than another character; this reflexive blame is recorded as a status effect on 'le narrateur' per the schema, though it could alternatively be read as narratorial commentary outside the interpersonal appraisal frame.
